title: terraform: unify private state layout for GPU node pools, IAM and networking (migration)
author: Diego Morales
body: Context: Private deployments require a consistent Terraform state layout across customers to enable modular upgrades and safe drift detection. Historically we kept GPU node pools, IAM bindings, and networking in separate state layouts which made cross-resource migrations brittle and increased manual intervention during upgrades. Motivation: unify the state layout for private deployments so the installer, helm charts, and terraform modules can perform automated migrations, reduce manual state moves, and make rollback safer. This PR: 1) introduces a unified state layout for private deployments that groups GPU node pools, IAM roles/policies, and VPC networking under a single private/<org>/<env> state namespace; 2) adds migration helpers (terraform state mv wrappers and import plans) and a `migrate_state.sh` driver to orchestrate migration in a preservation-first manner; 3) refactors the existing gpu_node_pools, iam, and networking modules to support both old and new state addresses via a compatibility layer; 4) updates examples and the private installer docs to outline the migration path; 5) adds an integration test harness that runs a dry-run migration against mocked state backends. Backwards compatibility: modules accept legacy address maps and will emit a terraform plan that is a no-op when run on already-migrated state. Migration path: run ./scripts/migrate_state.sh --preview to validate, then --apply to execute. For large orgs we recommend staging via a canary org and using the --partial flag to migrate one region at a time. Checklist: - [x] design review (ENG-3124) - [x] compatibility shim implemented - [x] migration driver script and dry-run - [x] integration tests for state transitions - [x] docs/upgrade guide updated - [x] e2e smoke on GCP and AWS emulators Notes for operators: the script requires read/write access to both old and new state backends and preserves all resource IDs. The migration intentionally avoids renaming resources that would force recreations; instead it creates aliased addresses and leaves legacy references intact until the operator confirms cutover. Risks and mitigation: the most likely failure mode is incomplete imports for manually managed IAM bindings; the script includes a --verify flag that runs aws/gcloud IAM checks post-migration. Rollback: a dry-run plan is generated before any state move; for state moves we keep snapshots in the same backend and output a restore command in the logs. Related: references to prior PRs and RFCs are in the description and the Linear ticket ENG-3124. Release notes: see release_notes field. CI: runs terraform fmt, tflint, unit module tests, integration migration dry-run; two intermittent integration tests were flakey in the first run and were fixed by adding exponential backoff in the migration driver. Merge: squashed after approvals, migration tests green, documented upgrade steps in docs/private/upgrade.md.

notes: This PR centralizes state layout to make future module upgrades and cross-resource rollouts safe. The compatibility shim keeps old addresses functional until operators complete the migration. Monitor IAM-bound services carefully during migration due to eventual consistency in cloud provider APIs.
